one_month_reasoning: Three scheduled events fall in the window. (1) 15 Oct: the South32 shareholder vote (12:00 AWST, before the US open). The board recommends the deal unanimously and the independent expert calls it fair and reasonable, so it will very likely pass with little price effect. (2) 15 Oct after the close: Alcoa's Q3 results. Consensus is about $1.52, down from $2.12, and the drop is well flagged. Guidance called for only small sequential changes. The Midwest premium held near $1.09/lb (CFO, 10 Sep), which is better than the stale 95c I used in round 1; Tower Extrusion's September Midwest average of $2.579/lb implies about $1.10 over LME. That trims my round-1 worry about the aluminium segment. (3) 28 Oct: the FOMC meeting, after a 25bp hike in September to 3.75-4.00%. Polymarket gives an October hike 37% and a hold 61% (30 Sep, about $17M volume). That is a modest dollar/commodity headwind but is now partly priced; I had wrongly called it 50-50 without a source in round 1. On the alternative data, China's social ingot inventory fell 118kt in the two weeks to 24 Sep to about 638kt, from a July peak of about 1.13Mt, which is supportive. Against that, LME on 29 Sep was cash $3,225 / 3M $3,231, so the backwardation of the spring has flipped into a slight contango. LME stocks are low (241kt, only 14.7kt cancelled), which signals physical tightness has eased but not reversed. Netting these out I see no directional edge, so I use a symmetric lognormal centred on $42 with a one-month sigma of 16.5% (56%/3.5 plus a little for the earnings day). I dropped my round-1 'technical breakdown / short accumulation' tilt because it had no source.

fair_value.method: Pro forma, assuming the South32 aluminium deal closes in H1 2027, before the horizon. Normalized combined 2027 EBITDA of about $3.1B (standalone about $2.3B, AliGroup about $0.78B, small synergies) x 5.0x = $15.5B EV. Subtract about $3.07B of net claims at Sep-27 (net debt $4.75B + pension $0.57B - Ma'aden stake about $1.25B - FCF about $1.0B) and divide by 282M diluted shares: about $44.1. Cross-check: EPS of $4.44 x 9x = $40, plus the Ma'aden stake at $4.4/share = $44.4. Blended: $44.

bear.story: EGA is at full output by Q1 2027, Alba restarts by mid-2027 and Hormuz normalizes. China's destock reverses after the holiday and Indonesia ramps up. The 2027 surplus reaches 1-1.5Mt and LME averages about $2,600, the Goldman downside. A Canada tariff deal pushes the Midwest premium below $0.80. Combined EBITDA falls to about $2.3B, which at 4.5x less about $3.2B of net claims is about $26.

base.story: LME averages $2,900-3,000. The South32 assets close in H1 2027 and the premium eases to about $1.00. Combined EBITDA is about $3.1B and FCF plus the Ma'aden stake keep net claims near $3B. At 5x the stock is about $44.

bull.story: Hormuz stays disrupted (Polymarket gave Hormuz normal by end-2026 only 20%), Gulf restarts slip, China holds its 45Mt cap and its stocks stay below 800kt. LME holds $3,300-3,500, the forward curve rather than the bank decks, and the premium stays above $1. Combined EBITDA of $4.2B+ at 5x, less about $2.7B of claims, gives about $65-70.

thesis_break_reason: At $27 the pro forma equity (282M shares) is about $7.6B. With about $3.1B of net claims after crediting the Ma'aden stake and the FCF, that implies EV of about $10.7B, about 3.4x my $3.1B normalized EBITDA. That only makes sense if LME is heading toward $2,500 with a collapsing Midwest premium, or if the AliGroup deal, the WA bauxite mine approvals or the balance sheet have gone wrong. It sits about 14% below the 52-week low of $31.45, outside ordinary 56%-vol noise around a fair value in the mid-$40s.

reasoning: Round 2 corrects three errors the supervisor found, and they largely offset. (a) My $3.5B combined EBITDA was too high. Rebuilt bottom-up from FY2025 standalone ($1.965B at about $2,630 LME) and LTM ($2.29B standalone, $3.15B pro forma), it is about $3.1B at a $2,950 deck: about -$9/share at 5x. (b) I left out the $1.36B Ma'aden stake; credited at $1.25B, that is about +$4.4/share. (c) Adding FCF to Sep-27 of about $1.0B (I had $0.8B) and the reported $0.57B pension (I had $0.65B) moves the claims slightly in my favour. The tax rate goes from 25% to 30%, which cuts EPS from $5.6 to $4.44. I lift the P/E multiple from 8x to 9x because the EPS is already normalized, but stop short of the supervisor's 10.5x and 5.25x because 2027 is likely a surplus year and leverage after the deal is about 1x. Net: fair value goes from $45 to $44, or 5% above spot. I fixed my lane: round 1 used only Polymarket as alternative data. This round adds physical and pricing trackers. China's social ingot stocks drew 118kt in two weeks to about 638kt (SMM via alcircle and Discovery Alert, two sources agreeing on direction). The LME 29 Sep tape shows the spring backwardation gone (cash-3M about $6 contango) with stocks at 241kt. Tower Extrusion's September Midwest average of $2.579/lb confirms a premium of about $1.10/lb. Polymarket and a news report put October Fed hike odds at 37%, replacing my unsourced 50-50. Together these say the physical market is still tight, China is drawing, but the acute squeeze has passed. That is roughly neutral against the bank decks, so I do not shift the deck. The distribution is a lognormal with median about $43.3 (a small drift toward the $44 fair value plus a little dividend), sigma 0.50, mixed 20% with sigma 0.62 for fatter tails from post-deal leverage and Gulf/Hormuz binaries. Scenarios at 25/50/25 ($26 / $44 / $68) have a mean of about $45.5, consistent with that. Research was limited: X/Reddit were not reachable, job-posting data was too thin to use, and Discovery Alert is a low-quality aggregator, so I only use it where SMM/alcircle agree.
